mission: MIRI is a Berkeley nonprofit that does research and public outreach to help prevent human extinction from artificial superintelligence. It helped found the field of AI alignment, but now says alignment is not on track to be solved in time. Its priority is persuading governments to agree a globally enforced halt on building superintelligence.

key_work.title: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies (book by Eliezer Yudkowsky & Nate Soares)
key_work.plain_summary: A popular book arguing that building superintelligence with anything like today's methods would very likely kill everyone, and that the world should stop before it does.

key_work.title: An International Agreement to Prevent the Premature Creation of Artificial Superintelligence
key_work.plain_summary: A draft treaty that would halt dangerous AI capability growth worldwide while still allowing today's safe AI uses, with ideas for how it could be verified.

key_work.title: AI Governance to Avoid Extinction: The Strategic Landscape and Actionable Research Questions
key_work.plain_summary: MIRI's research agenda for governance: it maps the possible paths ahead and lists the questions whose answers would most help reduce extinction risk.

key_work.title: What AI evaluations for preventing catastrophic risks can and cannot do
key_work.plain_summary: Argues that safety tests can show a model is dangerous but cannot prove it is safe, so evaluations should not be the main thing standing between us and catastrophe.

key_work.title: Corrigibility
key_work.plain_summary: An early formal look at how to build an AI that lets humans correct or shut it down, and why that is surprisingly hard to get right.

key_work.title: Logical Induction
key_work.plain_summary: A mathematical method for assigning sensible probabilities to unproven mathematical claims — part of MIRI's 'agent foundations' work on how ideal reasoners think.

warnings.text: If superintelligence is built any time soon with methods like today's, the most likely outcome is human extinction.
Technical progress on safety, alignment and control has failed to keep up with capabilities.
Nobody understands the inner workings of current AI well enough to fully control or steer it.
The companies building these systems cannot be relied on to stop in time.

recommendations.text: A globally coordinated, collectively enforced moratorium on developing superintelligence, as soon as possible and for as long as necessary.
An international agreement that halts dangerous capability growth while preserving access to today's safe AI applications.
Do not rely on evaluations as the main safety guarantee; they cannot rule out danger.
Build the technical and institutional capacity (e.g. compute monitoring) needed to enforce a halt.
